notes.text: 1. Time join. In the joined table, weather rows (on the hour) and logger rows (5, 20, 35 and 50 min past) interleave in time order and are never merged. Temperature is one column because both datasets use that name; wind is blank on logger rows and humidity on weather rows. Source names each row's dataset. The binned table averages every hour, so each row holds both datasets.

2. Same name, different measurement. The hive's temperature is not the air temperature, so in this node's panel it is set to 'Its own column'. The table shows temperature (A) and temperature (B) side by side, each blank on the other dataset's rows.

3. Stack mode. Neither time input is wired, so Join Data stacks the Control results, then the Treated results, each in their original order. Source is on by default when stacking and names each row's group; Group Comparison and the boxplot use it as the group for amplitude.

WORKFLOW: Join Data puts two datasets (A and B) in one set of columns. With a time wired for both, every row goes onto one time column, sorted and never merged; Bin Data then lines them up. With no time wired, it stacks A's rows and then B's. Columns with the same name share one column unless you choose 'Its own column'. Read the numbered notes.
